title: fix parallel column recovery race and test fixture taskpool leaks
body:
Addresses regression from:
- https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth2/pull/8346

This was periodically causing CI timeouts on, mostly, GitHub Actions Linux/amd64 runners. It would typically look like
```
2026-05-18T15:23:21.5438404Z DBG 2026-05-18 15:23:21.511+00:00 Received response from handler             status=400 meth=POST peer=127.0.0.1:35680 uri=/api/v1/eth2/sign/0xacf31f9b1ecf65dbb198e380599b6c81fc1a1f5db4457482cc697d81b1fdfb6e49cf8eff4980477f6e32749eef61dc4d content_type=text/plain content_size=45
2026-05-18T15:23:21.5439697Z 
2026-05-18T15:23:21.5439843Z EF - BPO forkdigests .......... (0.00s)
2026-05-18T15:23:29.1729143Z EF - KZG ............................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................. (4.05s)
2026-05-18T20:26:38.8829317Z ##[error]The operation was canceled.
2026-05-18T20:26:38.9063582Z Post job cleanup.
```
Or similar: it would finish the EF - KZG suite but not the PeerDAS KZG tests following it.

When eventually captured locally, the stack trace was:
```
/root/nimbus-eth2/tests/consensus_spec/test_fixture_kzg.nim(551): test_fixture_kzg
/root/nimbus-eth2/vendor/nim-unittest2/unittest2.nim(1175): test_fixture_kzg::runRecoverCellsAndKzgProofsParallelInvalidTest(string, string)
/root/nimbus-eth2/vendor/nim-unittest2/unittest2.nim(1095): unittest2::runDirect(unittest2::Test)
/root/nimbus-eth2/tests/consensus_spec/test_fixture_kzg.nim(468): runRecoverCellsAndKzgProofsParallelInvalidTest::runTestX60gensym899_(string, string)
/root/nimbus-eth2/vendor/nim-chronos/chronos/internal/asyncfutures.nim(1875): asyncfutures::waitFor(InternalRaisesFuture<Result<seq<kzg::KzgCellsAndKzgProofs>, cstring>, void>)
/root/nimbus-eth2/vendor/nim-chronos/chronos/internal/asyncfutures.nim(640): asyncfutures::pollFor(InternalRaisesFuture<Result<seq<kzg::KzgCellsAndKzgProofs>, cstring>, void>)
/root/nimbus-eth2/vendor/nim-chronos/chronos/internal/asyncengine.nim(1018): asyncengine::poll
/root/nimbus-eth2/vendor/nim-chronos/chronos/ioselects/ioselectors_epoll.nim(643): selectors2::selectInto2(Selector<asyncengine::SelectorData>, int, var<openArray<selectors2::ReadyKey> >)
```

It's also possible to intentionally widen the race window and cause it to happen nearly deterministically:
```nim
diff --git a/beacon_chain/spec/peerdas_helpers.nim b/beacon_chain/spec/peerdas_helpers.nim
index 99643bf5..a790f9b9 100644
--- a/beacon_chain/spec/peerdas_helpers.nim
+++ b/beacon_chain/spec/peerdas_helpers.nim
@@ -19,10 +19,11 @@ import
   ./crypto,
   ./[helpers, digest, column_map],
   ./datatypes/[fulu, deneb]
 
 from std/algorithm import sort
+from std/os import sleep
 from std/sequtils import anyIt, mapIt, repeat, toSeq
 from stew/staticfor import staticFor
 
 type
   CellBytes = array[fulu.CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, Cell]
@@ -207,10 +208,11 @@ proc recover_cells_and_proofs_parallel*(
       idxArr = cast[ptr UncheckedArray[CellIndex]](idxPtr)
       cellsArr = cast[ptr UncheckedArray[Cell]](cellsPtr)
     # Use toOpenArray to create views without copying
     defer:
       discard tsp.fireSync()
+      sleep(1)
 
     res[] = recoverCellsAndKzgProofsTask(
       idxArr.toOpenArray(0, columnCount - 1),
       cellsArr.toOpenArray(0, columnCount - 1)).valueOr:
         return false
```

The race involved `discard tsp.fireSync()` in each thread and `isReady`: https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth2/blob/279fd945ae7ee3b3a51d3d56a3beb80b14ec45e5/beacon_chain/spec/peerdas_helpers.nim#L285-L315

`workerRecover` is followed by effectively `readyWith` due to the [macro expansion](https://github.com/status-im/nim-taskpools/blob/4acdc6ef005a93dba09f902ed75197548cf7b451/taskpools/taskpools.nim#L478-L494):
```nim
    let asyncBody = quote do:
      # XXX: can't test that when the RootTask is default(Task) instead of a sentinel value
      # preCondition: not isRootTask(workerContext.currentTask.task)

      let res = `fnCallIdents`
      readyWith(`futFnParam`, res)

    let asyncFn = ident("taskpool_" & fnName)
    result.add nnkProcDef.newTree(
      asyncFn,
      newEmptyNode(),
      genericParams,
      asyncParams,
      nnkPragma.newTree(ident("nimcall")),
      newEmptyNode(),
      asyncBody
    )
```

So depending on which order the main thread observes the `readyWith` (`trySend`) and `fireSync` communications from the worker thread, e.g., if the main thread observes `fireSync` before `readyWith` has had a chance to be main-thread-observable, it can deadlock.

The tradeoff is allowing `sync` to block the main thread, typically briefly (microseconds) if at all. There are alternate approaches, but this is reasonable enough to unblock, CI, and it has to wait for all of them anyway; otherwise in the previous implementation it would run that recovery loop.

The missing `tp.shutdown()`s were mostly unrelated, but they did allow potential taskpool leakage.

title: Add `parent_block_root` to bid filtering key
body:
The gossip rule was changed from:

> [IGNORE] This bid is the highest value bid seen for the corresponding
>          slot and the given parent block hash

to:

> [IGNORE] this bid is the highest value bid seen for the tuple
>          (bid.slot, bid.parent_block_hash, bid.parent_block_root)`.

- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5001

This way, someone can't just abuse a reorg to bid a large amount on a non-canonical branch to purge the canonical bid. Catch up with spec.

Further, clean up the `parentExecHash != bid.parent_block_hash` check which is not from spec and rejected bids building on the timeline where the parent block's payload was withheld, by tracking the bids in the pool separately based on timeline.

body:
Looking at this `verifySidecars` in `storeBlock` timing on `geth-05` `unstable`:
```
geth-05% grep "block_processor verifySidecars completed" service.log | jq .verifySidecarsDur.value | tail -n1000 | shuf -n50 | sort -n

```
in nanoseconds, i.e. it's often taking 350+ milliseconds, which can push supernodes into resolving blocks too late.

This PR exploits that of the three paths by which columns arrive:
- `getBlobV2`/`getBlobsV3`/`getBlobsV4`: the EL is trusted, by spec. No further verification required;
- CL gossip: it already happened as part of gossip validation
- request manager: it does not validate fully, and therefore this validation does need to run

One can isolate the validation to only the request manager case, and in most cases avoid any further column validation at all as part of `storeBlock` and avoid these sometimes half-second additional delays in a hot path.

title: complete EMPTY/FULL sibling support in proto_array
body:
Follow-up to #8514.
This completes head selection and pruning for the EMPTY/FULL sibling nodes, matching alpha.9.

- Prune: rebuild the node array instead of chopping off the front. A block's FULL node is added whenever its payload arrives, which can be late and land after the finalized block. The old front-chop then kept that stray FULL node but deleted its index entry, crashing the `indices.len + fullBlockIndices.len == nodes.len` check.

- findHead: if a justified block's EMPTY node has no children because the chain continued on its FULL node, follow the FULL node's best descendant so head selection doesn't get stuck.

 - Tiebreak: choose between a block's EMPTY and FULL node by weight first, then by status (FULL beats EMPTY), matching [alpha.9](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-alpha.9/specs/gloas/fork-choice.md#modified-get_head), replacing the slot-based rule in #8514.
 
- applyScoreChanges takes an emptyPreferredRoot input that says when to prefer EMPTY for a block. The code that computes it (from PTC votes) lands in a later PR.
author: Tomi-3-0

title: route and validate gloas attestation votes in fork choice
body:
Makes attestation votes actually weight a block's EMPTY vs FULL node until now every vote landed on EMPTY because payload_present was never set and validates gloas attestations, matching alpha.9.

- process_attestation records the vote's payload preference, and compute_deltas routes the vote to the FULL node when it's a payload-present vote and that node exists, else EMPTY.
- on_attestation and process_block read the payload vote from `attestation.data.index` and thread it through.
- validate_on_attestation: data.index must be 0 or 1; a same-slot vote must be EMPTY; a full vote requires the payload to be known.

title: run newPayload on Fulu blocks concurrently with DA arrival
body:
This change affects only Fulu, neither Electra or earlier, nor Gloas or later. Neither has the latency issue involved. Currently, Nimbus:
1. receives a Fulu beacon block
2. waits for `enoughColumns` to arrive
3. sends the EL `newPayload`
4. when that returns `VALID`, resolves the block.

(2) and (3) do not overlap, currently. Pre-Fulu, blobs tended to arrive and be verified fairly quickly. Especially when waiting for 64 columns, this can readily require 2+s seconds, which leaves little time for some longer blocks to fully execute before running out of the 4s window.

So this PR changes the flow to:
1. receives a Fulu beacon block
2. sends the EL `newPayload`, which then runs in the background
3. waits for `enoughColumns` to arrive
4. when (2) and (3) both occur, resolves the block

There isn't a safety/security/EL DoS issue here: this PR specifically targets gossip traffic, and gossip validation already guarantees that each block is the first valid one per-proposer/slot to arrive.

title: add epbs fork-choice handlers into get_head and gossip
body:
Wires the ePBS fork-choice handlers into get_head, head selection, and gossip, so the node tracks each block's FULL vs EMPTY payload status and acts on it. get_head now returns the head together with its payload status.
  - get_head: gate proposer boost via should_apply_proposer_boost  proposer boost is applied only when `should_apply_proposer_boost` holds for the current slot; otherwise the boost root is zeroed. `get_head` returns (root, full) so callers know whether the head is the `FULL` or `EMPTY` variant.
  - find_head: compute emptyPreferredRoot ([should_extend_payload](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-alpha.10/specs/gloas/fork-choice.md#new-should_extend_payload)) implements the gloas variant tie-break
  - eth2_processor: feeds PTC messages to fork choice via `on_payload_attestation_message`,  payload-attestation gossip is now routed into the fork-choice backend, populating ptc_votes so is_payload_timely / the should_extend_payload tie-break have the data they need.
  -   Track weight per node (`pendingWeight`) and subtract it in the EMPTY-vs-FULL tie-break, mirroring `is_supporting_vote`

title: Init AttPool EpochRef every 1024 slots instead of every 1024 blocks
body:
As preparation for persisting all DAG heads in DB across restarts, prepare the initialization of the AttestationPool by extracting the per-head work into a helper. The performance optimization of #1910 in periods of long finality is slightly adjusted to ensure that calling the helper on extra heads produces monotonically increasing checkpoints.

Old logic fetches accurate checkpoints for the latest 256 blocks (from the head), and also every 1024 blocks (from the finalized).

New logic retains the former (eventually becomes union across all heads) and changes the second condition to the first block in each 1024 slot interval. This still skips most of the state replays but makes it so that if additional heads are imported, checkpoints increase at the same slot in each ancestry, i.e., on the first block introducing a new branch and at the first block entering a new 1024 slot interval.

Note that in situations that have lots of empty slots, this reduces startup performance compared to the old logic which only counted blocks, if there is nonfinality > 1024 slots (32 epochs, ~3.4 hours Mainnet).

title: unconditionally use EIP-7917-based proposer lookahead when projecting next proposal actions
body:

title: Ensure verification conditions for bid are satisfied as proposer
body:
Spec requires the proposer to ensure that the verification conditions in `process_execution_payload_bid` are satisfied in order to construct the `signed_execution_payload_bid` field in `BeaconBlockBody`:

https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-alpha.10/specs/gloas/validator.md#signed-execution-payload-bid

As gossip validation uses some arbitrary head state and also misses certain checks compared to the full verification conditions, bids that passed gossip validation may become invalid when re-verified with the correct state.

Re-verify external bid validity on proposal, and if invalid, fall back to local block building.

title: Reject bids with invalid prev_randao during gossip validation
body:
When someone sends us a bid with invalid prev_randao but high value, it kicks out the legitimate bid. The invalid one is also non-punishable as it fails subsequent state transition by peers.

Add an extra reject rule to filter out invalid prev_randao, there is only a single valid value for each parent block root, and we have efficient functionality in the blockchain_dag to obtain correct RANDAO without expensive state replays.

Also proposed for spec inclusion, but we'll need the rule regardless:

- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5360

Have moved this check to the end, because if the correct value has not yet been cached (i.e., no valid bid received), we may have to load the block from disk (once).

title: adjust slot end/next-slot-preparation timings
body:
Currently, slot end happens 5/6 through a slot (in 6 and 12s slots respectively, 5s and 10s) and preparation for the next slot begins at 11/12 through the slot (in 6s/12s respectively, 5.5s and 11s).

This needs adjustment for two reasons:
- in Gloas, currently PTC-related deadlines now happen 3/4 through the slot, so those now define the relatively idle tail of a slot, and the "slot end" is redefined in terms of those; and
- 1s before the end of a slot has proven borderline too slow to avoid slot start delays in some circumstances, especially around epoch boundaries which involve storing beacon states.

This PR instead redefines them as, slot end is 19/24 through the slot (4.75s and 9.5s respectively for 6s/12s slots) and next slot preparation at 7/8 through a slot (resp 5.25s and 10.5s), for an additional half-second in the 12s case.

Those Gloas deadlines are defined regardless already regardless of whether the node is in Gloas, so they're safe to use regardless of the current fork.

title: Fix slowlogs.py default threshold handling
body:
## Summary

Fix `scripts/slowlogs.py` so it can run without an explicit threshold argument.

The script defines a default threshold of `0.75`, but it previously checked `len(sys.argv) > 0` before reading `sys.argv[1]`. Since `sys.argv` always contains the script name, running the script without arguments raised an `IndexError` instead of using the default threshold.

## Changes

- Use the default threshold when no CLI argument is provided
- Preserve the existing custom threshold behavior

## Testing

- Verified default threshold behavior with sample log input
- Verified custom threshold behavior with `python3 scripts/slowlogs.py 0.25`

title: tune scoring params for Gloas topics
body:
Weights and rates are set by analogy to existing topics.

For weights, `payload_attestation` uses `0.5`, the same as `BeaconBlockWeight/AggregateWeight`, since PTC votes are consensus-critical, while bid and prefs use `0.05`, matching the minor announcement topics `VoluntaryExit/Slashing/BlsToExecutionChange`. 

 For rates (messages per slot), payload_attestation follows the same theoretical-max convention as SyncContribution, and prefs is set to 0.5. For bid, [the gossip layer only forwards a bid if it beats the highest one already seen for that slot](https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth2/blob/c0748e292da2a5eddeafc9ef0e8111cf473bd33e/beacon_chain/gossip_processing/gossip_validation.nim#L1897) , so only a handful should actually propagate per slot regardless of builder count; so a small constant (5.0) is used to reflect that.

Decay windows are matched to each topic's frequency, copied from the closest existing topic: `payload_attestation` uses 1 epoch (high-rate, like `AggregateProof`), bid uses 20 epochs (moderate, like `BeaconBlock`), and prefs uses 100 epochs (rare, like the slashing/exit topics).

title: Update fast_confirmation event to latest spec
body:
Specs added a `current_slot` marker to the `fast_confirmation` event:

> The node has executed the fast confirmation algorithm.
> This event should be emitted every time the algorithm is run,
> regardless of whether the most recent confirmed block has changed
> since the previous run. block is the root and slot is the slot of the
> most recent confirmed block, and current_slot is the wall-clock slot
> at which the algorithm was executed.

- https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Events/eventstream

Interpreting "every time the algorithm is run" as "whenever any of the data changed" to avoid redundant spam, and "wall-clock slot" as the slot to which fork choice was updated (may be slightly behind / ahead based on gossip clock disparity and lag spikes).

title: fix Gloas withdrawals predictions; quarantine Gloas columns arriving before block
body:
Whereas in Fulu, the columns refer [primarily to the parent block](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-alpha.11/specs/fulu/p2p-interface.md#new-data_column_sidecar_subnet_id):
```python
    # [IGNORE] The sidecar's block's parent has been seen
    # (MAY be queued for processing once the parent block is retrieved)
    if block_header.parent_root not in store.blocks:
        raise GossipIgnore("sidecar's parent has not been seen")

    # [REJECT] The sidecar's block's parent passes validation
    if block_header.parent_root not in store.block_states:
        raise GossipReject("sidecar's parent failed validation")
```

In Gloas they [refer to the current block](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-alpha.11/specs/gloas/p2p-interface.md), which means Gloas contains block/column races in a way Fulu doesn't.

Therefore, can't only use `ACCEPTED` columns in Gloas without dropping some. The column quarantine already had this `verified` vs not-`verified` structure, anticipating this distinction.

Been running this for a couple hours on `glamsterdam-devnet-6`. The column quarantine has caught 17 blocks arriving after some columns, which would have been previously dropped, and now are accounted for.

Also been comparing each predicted withdrawal with actual withdrawal and they've all matched.
author: tersec

title: fix: weigh justified EMPTY/FULL variants in get_head
body:
`findHead` picks the head by following the justified EMPTY node's `bestDescendant`, and consults the block's `FULL` variant if the `EMPTY` node had no descendants. when the `EMPTY` branch had any child at all, head selection followed the `EMPTY` chain and never weighed the `FULL` branch at all. 
Instead rank a block's `EMPTY` and `FULL` variants against each other by [`get_weight, get_payload_status_tiebreaker`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-alpha.11/specs/gloas/fork-choice.md#modified-get_head)).
author: Tomi-3-0

title: Skip zero ports when building peer dial addresses
body:
`toPeerAddr` builds dial multiaddrs from a peer's ENR. For a record advertising a `tcp`/`tcp6`/`quic`/`quic6` port of `0`, it produced an undialable `/ip4/x/tcp/0` (or `/udp/0` for QUIC) address and handed it to `switch.connect`, wasting a dial attempt (and, for static peers, retried).

Treat a zero port as absent for the TCP and QUIC dial transports, matching how the reference clients skip such records (e.g. go-ethereum's dialer returns `errNoPort`). The UDP branch is unchanged since it is not used for dialing.

Found during a cross-client discv5 audit; the same fix landed in Erigon's caplin sentinel (erigontech/erigon#22271).

Test added in `tests/test_discovery.nim`; it fails before the change (a `tcp=0` / `quic=0` record yields a dial address) and passes after.

title: bucket seen preferences by epoch mod (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 2)
body: The seen proposer-preferences cache used only 2 epoch buckets (mod 2), where three consecutive epochs should stay distinct. the cache needs room for 3 epochs worth of prefss at once: the one being wiped (`E-1`, current: `E`, and next: `E+1`). With only 2 buckets, the `E-1` and the `E+1` share one bucket , so wiping `E-1` also wipes `E+1` preferences

title: Clarify gossip limits
body:
In the spec, Req/Resp was changed a while ago to state that readers must not read more than max_compressed_len(n) bytes when processing framed snappy responses:

- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4045

The function for this limit is originally defined for non-framed snappy, but it leaves enough room to also support sensibly framed snappy, i.e., it is always possible to encode the response in a way so that it fits.

Still, this limit enables filtering data that is encoded maliciously, with lots of empty padding bytes, zero-length frames etc, while also not being too strict in case someone wraps subchunks of the response in separate snappy frames.

Note that there is also the 10 second response limit that applies to the entire chunk, so without this, it's also not unbounded how much spam can be sent.

title: RPC chunks with stricter DOS limits where possible
body:
Extra bytes beyond the `n` SSZ bytes in a Req/Resp request are required to invalidate the prior request:

- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/1606

Should be fine on all of Mplex, Yamux and Quic, i.e., the protocol requires the sender to explicitly half-close their end of the stream, so we can always read the EOF explicitly on the reading end.

If there's a disconnect between the end of the request or the EOF, the regular 10 second read timeout would eventually hit.

Impact is potentially a tiny higher latency before requests are answered as we wait for 1 more signal that may or may not be combined with the last request byte.

Closes #8435

title: Avoid duplicate fcU sending
body:
While light client is significantly ahead, its head overrides the head from forward sync when interacting with the ELs. That forward sync still triggers fcU periodically, though, which all get overridden with the same head information, leading to exact duplicates being sent.

This is changed to only send one duplicate per slot (still needed as the EL may be restarted or replaced in-between fcU calls). Also fix a race when switching over from the LC head to the forward sync head, where two fcU could be in flight simultaneously.

Closes #8041

title: Ensure sigsets are part of async env in batch validation
body:
(Patch was generated by Fable)

Since https://github.com/nim-lang/Nim/pull/23787:

> we lift only those locals that appear in more than one state

Therefore, the `let sigsets = batch[].multiSets.combineAll(verifier)` variable is only present in the stack, as it is not used anymore after the `await signal.wait()` further down.

To fix that, either we have to directly take an `addr` (or via template) but because we only do `baseAddr sigsets` it doesn't extend lifetime as that's just a regular `func` in stew.

Moving the section that converts the seq to unchecked array into the task fixes this, as the `task` is still used after the `await`.

Impact here is that some batch verifies may end up reporting a wrong result, and then fallback to the individual sig check. But we use refc so it's not deterministically hit.

https://github.com/nim-lang/Nim/issues/26041

title: networking: adapt gossip validators to nim-libp2p `Opt[seq[byte]]` payload
body:
## Summary
nim-libp2p master reworked the pubsub wire types (PR #2638, `chore(pubsub)!: protobuf_serialization`): `Message.data` changed from `seq[byte]` to `Opt[seq[byte]]`. Nimbus's `GossipMsg = messages.Message`, so both gossip validators in `eth2_network.nim` that read `message.data` (`.len`, `snappy.decode`) no longer typecheck. This adapts them and provisions the two new dependencies that libp2p master pulls in.

## What changed
- `beacon_chain/networking/eth2_network.nim`: in both `addValidator*` (sync) and `addAsyncValidator*` (async) `execValidator` procs, unwrap the payload once right after `inc nbc_gossip_messages_received` (`let data = message.data.get(newSeq[byte]())`) and use the local `data` for every prior `message.data` read. A missing payload maps to an empty seq, which `snappy.decode` turns into an empty result, routing to the existing `nbc_gossip_failed_snappy` / `ValidationResult.Reject` path — behaviour is unchanged for well-formed messages.
- Vendor `nim-libplum` at `acefbe42` (the pin declared in libp2p's `libp2p.nimble`). libp2p #2821 replaced nim-nat-traversal with nim-libplum; this mirrors that swap, matching the `ignore = untracked` convention nim-nat-traversal used.
- Bump `nim-lsquic` v0.5.4 → v0.6.0 (`d6d8f81`) for the per-dial certificate verification libp2p master requires.

## Depends on a nim-libp2p bump
This branch still pins `vendor/nim-libp2p` at `cb467731`, where `Message.data` is still `seq[byte]`, so the source change above does **not** compile against the current pin. Bumping `vendor/nim-libp2p` to a master commit that carries PR #2638 is tracked separately and must land together with (or before) this change for CI to go green.

## Risk
Gossip validation runs on attacker-controlled input; the change is defensive (a missing/empty payload is rejected, never unwrapped unchecked). New process attack surface comes from nim-libplum's bundled C library (UPnP/NAT-PMP/PCP), inherited from the upstream libp2p dependency swap.

## References
- nim-libp2p #2638 (pubsub protobuf_serialization), #2821 (nat-traversal → libplum), #2880 (3-arg dial)
- nim-lsquic v0.6.0 (`d6d8f81`)
author: gmelodie

title: Offload gossip KZG verifications to taskpool
body:
While processing KZG isn't as heavy as BLS, the timing of KZG gossip overlaps with attestation duties (Fulu) / payload attestations (Gloas). As soon as we received enough columns, the head event is sent to the VC but remaining data columns are still streaming in, potentially slowing down the submission of attestations, e.g., this should help with #7981.

As we already have the infrastructure for offloading the cryptographic verification work for other gossip topics, it's straightforward to just reuse the same machinery for KZG proofs. It's a bit simpler than BLS as we don't batch across columns, but follows the same flow.

title: Add version envelope to Gloas event stream events
body:
## Problem

Three Gloas event stream topics are specified to wrap their payload in a versioned envelope, but Nimbus emits the bare object:

| topic | Nimbus | spec |
|---|---|---|
| `execution_payload_bid` | `{"message":{...},"signature":"0x…"}` | `{"version":"gloas","data":{…}}` |
| `payload_attestation_message` | `{"validator_index":…,"data":{…},"signature":"0x…"}` | `{"version":"gloas","data":{…}}` |
| `proposer_preferences` | `{"data":{…}}` — no `version` | `{"version":"gloas","data":{…}}` |

Spec: [`apis/eventstream/index.yaml`](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/master/apis/eventstream/index.yaml).

Observed on `glamsterdam-devnet-7`. Lighthouse, Teku and Grandine all emit the specified form on the same network, so consumers reasonably assume the envelope is there. Dora, for example, fails every bid event with:

```
beacon block stream failed to decode execution_payload_bid event: unexpected end of JSON input
```

Its envelope unmarshal succeeds but yields a nil `data`, so the follow-up decode hits empty input.

## Cause

The generic `eventHandler` in `beacon_chain/rpc/rest_event_api.nim` calls `RestApiResponse.prepareJsonStringResponse(event)`. The only overload that writes `version` + `data` is constrained to `SomeForkedLightClientObject`; everything else falls through to `prepareJsonStringResponse(d: auto) = RestJson.encode(d)`.

The light client queues are declared as `AsyncEventQueue[RestVersioned[…]]` and so hit the versioned overload. `execPayloadBidQueue`, `payloadAttMsgQueue` and `proposerPreferencesQueue` hold raw types and lose the envelope.

## Fix

- Wrap the three queues in `RestVersioned[T]`, matching `finUpdateQueue` / `optUpdateQueue`.
- Add a `prepareJsonStringResponse` overload for a new `SomeVersionedEventObject` typeclass covering the three payload types. It is disjoint from `SomeForkedLightClientObject`, so no overload ambiguity.
- Derive `jsonVersion` / `sszContext` from the relevant slot (bid `message.slot`, payload attestation `data.slot`, `message.proposal_slot`) via `consensusForkAtEpoch` / `forkDigestAtEpoch` rather than hardcoding `gloas`.
- Drop `EventProposerPreferencesObject`, which existed only to produce `{"data":…}` and is superseded by `RestVersioned`.

No wire change for any other topic.

## Testing

Builds clean (`make nimbus_beacon_node`, binary reports `v26.7.0-9f2756` matching this commit).

Verified the emitted shape directly by serialising each of the three payload types through the new overload:

```
BID: {"version":"gloas","data":{"message":{"parent_block_hash":"0x00…","slot":"0",…},"signature":"0x00…"}}
PAM: {"version":"gloas","data":{"validator_index":"0","data":{"beacon_block_root":"0x00…",…},"signature":"0x00…"}}
PP:  {"version":"gloas","data":{"message":{"dependent_root":"0x00…","proposal_slot":"0",…},"signature":"0x00…"}}
```

All three now match the spec envelope. Expected shape cross-checked against Lighthouse/Teku/Grandine output on `glamsterdam-devnet-7`.

title: Support recent stateRoot in more beacon-APIs
body:
Nimbus db doesn't support looking up historical states by state_root, but recent state roots are available in the BeaconState already in RAM, and getBlockSlotId actually supports looking them up.

Allow querying by recent state roots (8192, based on head BeaconState) and fix error code which should be 404 if not found instead of 500. The functionality is available, just not exposed.

We still can't provide these APIs for historical states, but they are available by slot. Further, only canonical states according to fork choice are available by state_root.

Closes #7832

title: Pre-heat shuffling cache for next next epoch at last slot in epoch

title: fix(vc): ignore unscheduled fork timing skew across beacon nodes
body:
## Summary
- Canonicalize Gloas/Heze-only `TimeParams` fields to local defaults when those forks are still `FAR_FUTURE`, so VC startup no longer fails if beacon nodes disagree on draft constants such as `PAYLOAD_DUE_BPS` (alpha.11 `7500` vs alpha.12 `5000`).
- Once a fork is scheduled, those fields still require cross-BN agreement.
- Improve the incompatible-time-config warning to log which `TimeParams` fields differ.
- Add unit coverage for the unscheduled vs scheduled comparison behavior.

Fixes #8833

## Motivation
Nimbus VC compares full `TimeParams` from every configured beacon node's `/eth/v1/config/spec` during `initTimeConfig()`. Gloas timing keys like `PAYLOAD_DUE_BPS` are already exposed before Gloas is scheduled, and clients currently ship different draft values. That causes multi-client VC setups (e.g. Nimbus/Teku, or Lodestar1.46-rc.0/Lighthouse/Grandine) to fail startup with `Could not obtain time configuration parameters`, even though runtime compatibility only checks slot duration.

## Test plan
- [x] Added unit tests in `tests/test_validator_client.nim` covering:
  - unscheduled Gloas: `PAYLOAD_DUE_BPS` 7500 vs 5000 canonicalizes to equal `TimeParams`
  - scheduled Gloas: same disagreement remains unequal and is described in the diff helper
- [ ] CI `test_validator_client` / unit suite
- [ ] Manual: VC with Lodestar (`PAYLOAD_DUE_BPS=5000`) + Lighthouse/Nimbus (`7500`) while `GLOAS_FORK_EPOCH` is far-future should start successfully

## AI assistance disclosure
I used Cursor (Composer) to help inspect the Nimbus VC startup path, draft this patch, and prepare the PR text. I reviewed the resulting diff and intend it as a proposed fix for #8833 / the Lodestar interop case discussed there. I'm a node operator rather than a regular Nimbus contributor, so corrections from maintainers are welcome.

title: Emit head event also when there was a reorg
body: Spec is a bit vague but https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/117 description clarifies that the head event should also be sent for reorg. This way, VCs subscribed only to 'head' can detect reorgs more quickly.
author: etan-status

title: Monitor head event instead of block event in VC
body: Head event is sent once BN has selected new head for AttestationData. Block event is slightly too early (although practically, by the time that the VC requests the AttestationData, head is most likely selected). Switching to head event also allows reacting to reorgs more quickly.
author: etan-status

title: Refresh VC duties when 'head' event reports new dependent roots
body:
The VC now tracks which dependent root was used most recently for duties updates, so that reorgs that solely drop duties without adding new ones can also be logged, i.e., when a proposer duty is scheduled but later dropped by a reorg, the reorg message now also shows up, whereas before the log would only display when the duty gets _replaced_ by a new one.

In 'event' mode, when a 'head' event containing conflicting dependent root information is detected, duties are refreshed immediately instead of waiting for the next slot, in line with [beacon-APIs recommendations](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/master/apis/validator/duties/attester.yaml):

> Duties should only need to be checked once per epoch, however a chain reorganization (of > MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD epochs) could occur, resulting in a change of duties. For full safety, you should monitor head events [...]

While subscribed to events (`BlockMonitoringType.Event`), duties are only polled once per epoch, or when they get invalidated. They are still only requested at most once per slot, so the maximum load on the BN is shared with the `poll` method.

The `poll` method is unchanged and still polls every slot unconditionally.

Closes #7830

title: Initialize ValidatorMonitor counter metrics to 0 on start
body:
From https://prometheus.io/docs/practices/instrumentation/#avoid-missing-metrics

> Time series that are not present until something happens are difficult
> to deal with, as the usual simple operations are no longer sufficient
> to correctly handle them. To avoid this, export a default value such
> as 0 for any time series you know may exist in advance.

Initialize the "_totals" metric on startup (default), or initialize the per-pubkey metrics on registration (with `--validator-monitor-details`). That way, they get initialized as early as possible, rather than on the first time where they are incremented.

Closes #7802

title: sync: reset queue when failed request empties head
body:
## Summary

Fix a SyncQueue liveness condition where removing a failed request can leave
the current queue head with no active requests while later workers remain
blocked in `push()`.

Those blocked workers can continue holding their acquired peers. If all
remaining peers are held this way, no peer is available to refill the missing
head range, preventing synchronization from making further progress.

When removing a failed request empties the current queue head,
`clearAndWakeup()` resets the speculative queue and wakes blocked pushes. This
lets those workers return and release their peers so the missing head range can
be requested again.

## Regression tests

Adds forward and backward tests covering the case where:

- the sole request at the queue head fails;
- later requests have already completed;
- later `push()` calls are blocked behind the head;
- removing the failed head must release those blocked pushes.

Without the production change, both new tests fail.

With the change on current `unstable`:

- `tests/test_sync_manager.nim`: 27/27 pass
- repeated execution of the same test binary: 30/30 pass

The same fix and regression-test pair was also validated on Nimbus v26.7.0.

## Real-world validation

The issue was encountered while testing Nimbus on a private Ethereum PoS
network.

A patched v26 beacon node was subsequently tested from fresh consensus and
execution databases with a hard limit of 3 consensus peers. It completed
approximately 1.05 million slots of historical backfill while continuing to
follow the live chain, matched an independent Lighthouse node at finality, and
remained healthy for more than 2.5 hours after backfill completion.

The historical INFO logs do not contain enough detail to prove the exact
initiating request from the original incident, so this PR does not claim that
exact historical trigger. The regression tests target the generic liveness
condition reproduced independently.

title: fix: write generated jwt.hex with 0600 permissions
body:
When `--jwt-secret` is omitted, `checkJwtSecret` generates `dataDir/jwt.hex` with `std/os.writeFile`. That uses the process umask (typically 0644). Anyone who can read the data directory can mint Engine API JWTs.

Validator keystores already go through `secureWriteFile` (0600 on Unix, user-only ACL on Windows). Use the same helper for the generated JWT secret. Failure still warns and continues, same as today.

#7533 tried this against `stable` and the bot closed it. This is the current `unstable` generate path.

## Test

Static: `secureWriteFile` is `writeFile(..., 0o600)` in `beacon_chain/filepath.nim`. The old call is two-arg `writeFile` (umask default). I do not have a Nim toolchain here to run `tests/test_el_conf`.

title: Validate bid gas limit against the payload at bid.parent_block_hash
body:
## What

`validateExecutionPayloadBid` derived `parent_gas_limit` from `dag.headState.latest_execution_payload_bid.gas_limit` — the head block's own bid — regardless of which payload the bid builds on. The spec keys the check on the payload the bid actually extends:

```python
parent_gas_limit = seen.execution_payloads[bid.parent_block_hash].gas_limit
```
(https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/a670e0193446474bb1775ec94a93ca6fbaa11a89/specs/gloas/p2p-interface.md#L995-L1000)

A bid with `parent_block_root = head` and `parent_block_hash = head_bid.parent_block_hash` (head payload treated as withheld — permitted by `is_bid_compatible_with_head` when `should_build_on_full` is false) must be checked against the grandparent payload's gas limit. Whenever the gas limit is moving, that differs from the head bid's gas limit by one EIP-1559 step, so a spec-correct bid was dropped with `gas limit not target-compatible` — on gossip and via `POST /eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_bids` (same path).

This PR resolves the block carrying the payload identified by `bid.parent_block_hash` via the existing `dag.executionParent(parentBlck, bid.parent_block_hash)` (same lookup `validateBeaconBlockGloas` uses), and uses that block's committed gas limit (`loadExecutionGasLimit`: the bid's `gas_limit` post-Gloas, the payload's pre-Gloas). Envelopes must match their bid's `gas_limit`, so the bid value is the payload value.

## Why

Seen on glamsterdam-devnet-8 (gas limit ramping under EIP-8261). Slot 85165: payload at 85163 had gas limit 199411976, payload at 85164 (head) had 199606713, target 200000000. A builder's parent-empty bid carried 199606713 = 199411976 + 199411976/1024 − 1, correct for the payload it builds on; comparing against the head bid (199606713) instead makes it look like it failed to step toward the target.

Same class of bug was found in prysm (fixed in https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17405), lighthouse (https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/pull/9905) and grandine; lodestar and teku are correct. The spec gossip test vectors don't cover empty-head bids yet (all cases use the head's own payload as `parent_block_hash`), a vector PR is in progress.

## Notes

- Builds `nimbus_beacon_node` locally; there is no existing unit-test harness for `validateExecutionPayloadBid`, happy to add one if you can point me at the preferred fixture.

title: config: load networking overrides from RuntimeConfig
body:
## Summary

Make the remaining networking parameters available through Nimbus's typed `RuntimeConfig` path instead of requiring compile-time overrides:

- `EPOCHS_PER_SUBNET_SUBSCRIPTION`
- `SUBNETS_PER_NODE`
- `MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY`

The `MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS` and `TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH` portions from earlier revisions are no longer part of this branch; those were subsumed upstream by #9074.

This remains network-agnostic: it adds no custom-network branches, chain IDs, names, or magic values.

## Design

Runtime consumers use typed `RuntimeConfig` fields; stock defaults remain unchanged.

`MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY` is propagated through the current gossip, light-client, peer-protocol, execution-payload, and validator-REST paths.

Stability-subnet behavior uses runtime `EPOCHS_PER_SUBNET_SUBSCRIPTION` and `SUBNETS_PER_NODE`.

`ActionTracker` precomputes the per-session node offset once during initialization and stores it as `uint64`, so recurring stability-subnet computation no longer performs `UInt256` div/mod arithmetic.

`SUBNETS_PER_NODE = 0` is accepted and simply produces no stability-subnet subscriptions. The RuntimeConfig compatibility boundary retains the upper bound at `ATTESTATION_SUBNET_COUNT`.

## Tests

Permanent regressions cover:

- compiled networking defaults
- custom runtime networking values
- compatibility handling including `SUBNETS_PER_NODE = 0`
- runtime stability-subnet parameters

Final review-specific validation on commit `07c1509ff1310133d1754aafb237713eed292b16`:

- full `nimbus_beacon_node` build passed with `-d:disableMarchNative -d:disableLTO`
- `all_tests`: **1,009 tests**, **998 OK**, **0 failed**, **0 errors**, **11 skipped**
- final `git diff --check` passed
- no diff remains for `MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS` or `TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH`

The preceding post-#9074 full local qualification also passed:

- consensus-spec minimal: 8,366 tests, 0 failed
- consensus-spec mainnet: 6,428 tests, 0 failed
- `all_tests`: 1,009 tests, 0 failed
- `block_sim`, `fork_choice`, `proto_array`, `test_libnimbus_lc`, and `process_state`: passed

title: sync: preserve peer availability during status refresh
body:
## Summary

- avoid the status-refresh throttle when a worker owns the final available sync peer
- preserve the existing anti-stampede delay while another peer remains available
- add regression coverage for fresh/stale status with zero/one remaining available peer

## Problem

`getOrUpdatePeerStatus` runs after a worker has acquired a peer. When the cached status is still fresh, the current code sleeps before refreshing it.

Under low-peer conditions, workers can each retain a peer while sleeping in this throttle. If the final available peer is retained this way, the pool can temporarily have no peer available for other sync workers, preventing forward progress.

## Change

Delay only when both conditions hold:

1. the peer status is still fresh enough for the existing throttle; and
2. at least one other sync peer remains available in the pool.

When the current worker owns the final available peer, refresh its status immediately instead of sleeping while holding that peer.

The existing anti-stampede behavior is otherwise unchanged.

## Tests

Added a regression test covering all four policy cases:

- fresh status, 0 other peers available -> do not delay
- fresh status, 1 other peer available -> delay
- stale status, 0 other peers available -> do not delay
- stale status, 1 other peer available -> do not delay

Validation on the current `unstable` base:

- `tests/test_sync_manager.nim`: 26/26 passed
- the same focused test binary was then run 30 additional times: 30/30 passed
- full `nimbus_beacon_node` build passed

The underlying low-peer behavior was also reproduced separately in a controlled two-peer A/B: the unpatched implementation could retain both peers in status refresh and stop making progress, while the patched implementation recovered and remained live.

This is intentionally a small change to the current sync manager. I am aware that #7921 is reworking the syncing subsystem; if that work replaces this path, the regression scenario should still be useful when checking equivalent peer-retention behavior.

title: fix(vc): skip produceAttestationData when no attester duties
body:
## Summary
- Do not call `produceAttestationData` (or wait for attestation-due) when the slot has no attester duties.
- Matches Lodestar, Teku, Lighthouse, and Prysm, and matches the honest-validator spec (attest on the assigned slot only).
- Stops idle-slot BN/middleware timeouts and “Beacon node down” log spam.
Lighthouse hit the same every-slot fetch after an Electra refactor and fixed it in [sigp/lighthouse#8559](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/pull/8559) (“Do not request attestation data when attestation duty is empty”).

## Problem
The attestation service runs every slot. With no attester duty it still waited until attestation-due and called `GET /eth/v1/validator/attestation_data`. That is not required by the spec: a validator attests once per epoch on the slot from `get_committee_assignment`, which returns `None` when there is no assignment ([phase0 honest validator — Attesting](https://ethereum.github.io/consensus-specs/specs/phase0/validator/#attesting)).
Against a local BN this is wasted traffic. Against Obol Charon the endpoint **blocks on DutyDB** until the cluster has attestation data for a real duty, so an idle slot never returns. The VC then times out and flaps the node:
Against a local BN this is wasted traffic. Against Obol Charon the endpoint **blocks on DutyDB** until the cluster has attestation data for a real duty, so an idle slot never returns. The VC then times out and marks the beacon node down (it is logged online again shortly after):
```
t+0.000s  INF  Slot start        node_status=synced delay=~2ms
t+7.5s    WRN  Beacon node down  reason="Timeout exceeded … produceAttestationData(best)"
t+7.5s    WRN  Unable to proceed attestations  duties_count=0  service=attestation_service
```
`duties_count=0` means no attester duty *this slot* (`Slot start` also shows `attestationIn` many minutes away).  On a duty slot the same path publishes normally (~50ms after attestation-due).

## Approach
In `spawnAttestationTasksV2`, return immediately when `getAttesterDutiesForSlot` is empty.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests in `tests/test_validator_client.nim` for `getAttesterDutiesForSlot`: empty map, duty on another slot, duty on the requested slot
- [x] CI unit suite / `test_validator_client`

## AI assistance disclosure

I used Cursor to help inspect the Nimbus VC attestation loop, compare other clients and the honest-validator spec, draft this patch, and prepare this PR text. I reviewed the resulting diff and can explain the change. A human author remains responsible for the submitted code (see Status/Logos contributor guidance on AI-assisted work: allowed for drafting; the opener must review, verify, and be able to explain every change; PRs should not be opened automatically by an agent/bot). I am a node operator rather than a regular Nimbus contributor; corrections from maintainers are welcome.

title: fix(vc): decode GAS_LIMIT_SCHEDULE arrays in getSpec
body:
## Summary
- Accept `GAS_LIMIT_SCHEDULE` from Beacon API `GET /eth/v1/config/spec` as a JSON array (same path as `BLOB_SCHEDULE`) in VC `VCRuntimeConfig` decoding.
- Stops Nimbus VC from failing getSpec decode when a BN returns `GAS_LIMIT_SCHEDULE: []` or a populated schedule, which was flapping the BN Online/Offline.
- Adds a REST serialization unit test and refreshes `AllTests-mainnet.md` (`all_tests` path) per Nimbus CI expectations.

## Problem
Beacon API `getSpec` returns array-valued config keys as JSON arrays. Nimbus VC only allowlisted `blob_schedule` as non-string, so Lodestar (and any BN) returning `GAS_LIMIT_SCHEDULE` as `[]` or with entries failed decode.

This showed up against Lodestar `v1.47.0`, which always exposed `GAS_LIMIT_SCHEDULE` from getSpec (including empty on mainnet). Related Lodestar change and discussion:

- Lodestar PR: https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10004 — temporary omit-until-Gloas interop guard on Lodestar’s side
- Review note from nflaig: https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10004#discussion_r3942033465 — lasting fix belongs on Nimbus (parse/allowlist array-valued `GAS_LIMIT_SCHEDULE` like `BLOB_SCHEDULE`); Lodestar returning an array matches the API / consensus-spec shape

Consensus-spec mainnet config includes `GAS_LIMIT_SCHEDULE: []`; clients that emit the field as a JSON array are correct. The durable interop fix is VC-side decoding.

## Approach
In `beacon_chain/spec/eth2_apis/eth2_rest_json_serialization.nim`, treat `gas_limit_schedule` like `blob_schedule` when reading `VCRuntimeConfig`.

## Test plan
- [x] Unit test in `tests/test_eth2_rest_serialization.nim`: empty and populated `BLOB_SCHEDULE` / `GAS_LIMIT_SCHEDULE`, plus wrapped `GetSpecVCResponse`
- [x] Ran `all_tests` (new test OK); refreshed `AllTests-mainnet.md` with the new REST suite line

## AI assistance disclosure

I used Cursor to help inspect getSpec / `VCRuntimeConfig` decoding, cross-check Lodestar#10004 and the Beacon API array behavior, draft this patch and tests, regenerate `AllTests-mainnet.md`, and prepare this PR text. I reviewed the resulting diff and can explain the change. A human author remains responsible for the submitted code (see Status/Logos contributor guidance on AI-assisted work: allowed for drafting; the opener must review, verify, and be able to explain every change; PRs should not be opened automatically by an agent/bot). I am a node operator rather than a regular Nimbus contributor; corrections from maintainers are welcome.

title: Support import of pre-Capella state after post-Capella init
body:
Pre-Capella states in don't store their withdrawal credentials in the database and rely on the shared immutableValidators list. Closes #7527

title: avoid hang on missing block on epoch boundary
body:
Observed on `glamsterdam-devnet-8`.

https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth2/blob/47e7cfa5a48477cb77f26c451abc0e20fe866e2b/beacon_chain/sync/sync_dag.nim#L499-L502 got stuck in an infinite loop due to a block that was its own parent:
```
DBG 2026-09-11 12:19:13.655+00:00 Got finalized head event                   topics="sync" block_root=7bf94350 state_root=c7769600 epoch=6526 checkpoint=6526:7bf94350 parent_root=7bf94350 block_slot=208832 last_seen_epoch=6525
DBG 2026-09-11 12:19:13.655+00:00 Got finalized head event, which is not known topics="sync" block_root=7bf94350 state_root=c7769600 epoch=6526 checkpoint=6526:7bf94350 parent_root=7bf94350 block_slot=208832
```

https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/208832 was a missed block (by `nimbus-reth-1`, incidentally) on epoch 6526's boundary.

https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth2/blob/47e7cfa5a48477cb77f26c451abc0e20fe866e2b/beacon_chain/sync/sync_dag.nim#L504-L507 has the same structural issue in that it doesn't detect cycles. It just didn't happen to be the one encountered first, so it wasn't where this hang occurred.

The main fix in this PR is in `beacon_chain/sync/sync_overseer2.nim`, with which Floyd's cycle-finding algorithm shouldn't be necessary. That is, `dag.finalizedHead.slot` became 208832, so `let parentBid = dag.getBlockIdAtSlot(slot - 1)` became 208831, which was the block's own slot, creating the circularity, so that should prevent cycles for any other parent iteration downstream too.

[nimbus.log.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32157303/nimbus.log.gz) has complete debug logs from node launch.

title: use beacon block gossip validation test vectors
body:
Among other changes, this removes a gossip validation change added by
- #8486

and the tests which enforce it, supplanted entirely by the new consensus spec reference test vectors introduced by
- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5294

In particular, https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5294 replaces
> - _[IGNORE]_ The block's parent execution payload (defined by
>  `bid.parent_block_hash`) has been seen (via gossip or non-gossip sources) (a
>  client MAY queue blocks for processing once the parent payload is retrieved).
> - If `execution_payload` verification of block's execution payload parent by an
>  execution node **is complete**:
> - [REJECT] The block's execution payload parent (defined by
>    `bid.parent_block_hash`) passes all validation.

with
```python
    # [New in Gloas:EIP7732]
    # [IGNORE] If the parent block is full, the parent payload is valid
    # (MAY be queued until the parent payload is verified)
    if is_parent_node_full(store, block):
        if not is_payload_verified(store, block.parent_root):
            raise GossipIgnore("parent payload is not verified")

   # ...

    # [New in Gloas:EIP7732]
    # [REJECT] If the parent is not full, the bid builds on the parent's execution head
    if not is_parent_node_full(store, block):
        if bid.parent_block_hash != parent_state.latest_block_hash:
            raise GossipReject("bid does not build on the parent's execution head")
```
in probably the closest functional analogue, so somewhat dodges this genesis special case.

It still notes that
```nim
      if executionParent.slot != GENESIS_SLOT:
        envelopeQuarantine[].addMissing(executionParent.root)
```
so avoids certain nonsense quarantine actions.

[`test_gossip_beacon_block__ignore_parent_payload_not_verified`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-beta.0/tests/core/pyspec/eth_consensus_specs/test/gloas/networking/test_gossip_beacon_block.py#L141-L185) is the specific test which doesn't pass otherwise, because due to
```nim
    elif executionParent.slot != GENESIS_SLOT and
        not dag.db.containsExecutionPayloadEnvelope(executionParent.root):
      return ignore here
```
it was simply gated off.

title: docs: remove dead multinet path and GitPOAP badge
body:
## Summary

README currently points readers at two dead resources:

1. **multinet tooling link** — `https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth2/tree/master/multinet` is gone on both `stable` and `unstable` (multinet was removed from this repo years ago; eth-clients/multinet is archived).
2. **GitPOAP badge** — `public-api.gitpoap.io` / `www.gitpoap.io` / `gitpoap.io` no longer resolve (NXDOMAIN), so the badge is a broken image and dead outbound link.

This PR removes both from `README.md` only.

## Repro

**Dead multinet path (404):**
```bash
curl -sI "https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth2/tree/master/multinet" | head -1
# HTTP/2 404

# Or via Contents API on stable tip:
gh api repos/status-im/nimbus-eth2/contents/multinet?ref=stable
# {"message":"Not Found",...}
```

**GitPOAP NXDOMAIN:**
```bash
host gitpoap.io
# Host gitpoap.io not found: 3(NXDOMAIN)

host www.gitpoap.io
# Host www.gitpoap.io not found: 3(NXDOMAIN)

host public-api.gitpoap.io
# Host public-api.gitpoap.io not found: 3(NXDOMAIN)
```

## Changes

- Remove the Tooling bullet that linked to the removed `multinet` tree path.
- Remove the GitPOAP badge/link from the README header badges.

title: docs: replace dead lasca SoK PDF link in cpu_features
body:
## Summary
In `docs/cpu_features.md`, the SoK citation PDF hosted at `lasca.ic.unicamp.br` now returns **HTTP 404**. This PR replaces it with a Wayback Machine snapshot that still returns **HTTP 200** `application/pdf`.

**Base branch: `unstable`** (PRs targeting `stable` are auto-closed).

Docs-only; does not touch README multinet/GitPOAP.

## File
- `docs/cpu_features.md`

## Repro

```bash
# Original host 404
curl -sI https://www.lasca.ic.unicamp.br/media/publications/p9-faz-hernandez.pdf | head -1
# HTTP/2 404

# Wayback mirror 200 PDF
curl -sI http://web.archive.org/web/20250418104712/https://www.lasca.ic.unicamp.br/media/publications/p9-faz-hernandez.pdf | head -5
# HTTP/1.1 200 OK
# Content-Type: application/pdf

# Present on unstable tip
gh api repos/status-im/nimbus-eth2/contents/docs/cpu_features.md?ref=unstable -q .sha
```

Same paper is also identified by ACM DOI `10.1145/3197507.3197511` (optional cross-reference; link change above is sufficient for readers).

title: fix(era): parse filenames for hyphenated network names
body:
`Era.fromEraFile` recovers the era number from an era file by splitting the whole
file name on `-` and requiring exactly three parts (`ncli/era.nim`):

```nim
let parts = name.split("-")
if parts.len == 3 and parts[0] == cfg.name() and name.endsWith(".era") and parts[1].len == 5:
```

`CONFIG_NAME` is free-form and explicitly allowed to contain `-` - in
`beacon_chain/spec/presets.nim` it is documented as `# Must match the regex: [a-z0-9\-]` -
and `docs/e2store.md` specifies the era file naming convention as
`<config-name>-<era-number>-<short-historical-root>.era` using that same field. The
generator half of the pair agrees and happily produces such names:

```nim
&"{cfg.name()}-{era.uint64:05}-{shortLog(eraRoot)}.era"
```

So with `CONFIG_NAME = my-testnet`, `eraFileName` produces the valid name
`my-testnet-00012-xxxxxxxx.era`, the parser splits it into four parts, `parts.len == 3`
fails, and the file is rejected. This is not limited to the CLI - anything that reads
a network's era directory is affected:

* `EraFile.eras` skips every such file while walking the era directory
  (`beacon_chain/era_db.nim`), so `getEraFile`, `genesis`, `latest` and era-based
  backfill all silently see an empty directory
* `ncli db verifyEra` refuses the file with
  `name does not match {network}-{era:05d}-{root}.era` (`ncli/ncli_db.nim`)

Fix by stripping the known network prefix and the `.era` extension first, and only
then splitting the remaining `<era>-<root>` on its single separator, so that hyphens in
the network name are no longer mistaken for field separators.

While here, the era number is accepted as five digits *or more* rather than exactly
five: `eraFileName` zero-fills with `:05`, which is a minimum width, so era numbers of
six digits or more are generated but cannot currently be parsed back. This is far in
the future (roughly 312 years of eras for mainnet) but the parser should simply accept
what the generator can emit.

Tests: new `tests/test_era.nim` (wired into `tests/all_tests.nim`) covers the
`eraFileName` -> `fromEraFile` round-trip for networks with and without hyphens, era
numbers above five digits, and rejection of foreign and malformed file names. On the
unpatched parser these fail; with the fix they pass.

Behaviour change worth noting: a file name with an empty root such as
`mainnet-00012-.era` is now rejected - previously it parsed as era 12. Such names
cannot be produced by `eraFileName` (`shortLog` always yields eight hex characters)
and carrying an empty root is meaningless, but I'm happy to relax that check if you'd
rather keep the parser maximally permissive.

title: Bump urllib3 from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0 in /docs
body:
Bumps [urllib3](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3) from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0.
Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's releases.

2.8.0

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Security

Fixed the following security issues:

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)

[!IMPORTANT] urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that behavior may require changes.

Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with proxy_assert_hostname or proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy connections.

[!NOTE] CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.

Deprecations & Removals

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)

Features

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the result of parse_url(). (#4945)
  • Added basic_auth_encoding and proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)

Bugfixes

  • Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112, preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as Set-Cookie. (#1362)

  • Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with ProxyManager when use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)

  • Changed behavior of the default ConnectionPool.pool initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the queue module after the ConnectionPool is instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls class property. This is done because sometimes the queue.LifoQueue is monkey-patched late in the program, such as by gevent. (#3289)

  • Raised UnrewindableBodyError instead of ValueError when retrying a request whose body had tell() but not seek(). (#3779)

  • Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating with the proxy server. (#3785)

  • Fixed HTTPResponse.drain_conn() to discard unread response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt when doing HTTPResponse.stream(...)). (#5019)

  • Fixed is_ipaddress() to detect non-standard IPv4 forms accepted by socket.connect, such as hex (0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), and decimal integers (2130706433), ensuring SSL certificate verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen raising a misleading FullPoolError instead of ValueError when called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created with block=True. (#5059)

  • Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit :0 values instead of substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool selection, proxy configuration, connection_from_url(), and HTTP/2 request authority. (#5071, #5101)

  • Fixed a bug where PoolManager passed the assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint parameters to HTTP connection pools. (#5077)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and HTTP proxy forwarding to strip URL fragments from absolute request targets before sending requests. (#5079)

  • Added safeguards to the proxy tunneling code to prevent potential security issues when handling invalid characters in the proxy host and HTTP headers. This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and Python 3.12 when the standard library does not contain the fix; those on newer Python versions should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the same security fixes. (#5091)

  • Fixed HTTPSConnection.connect() overriding ProxyConfig.ssl_context's certificate policy and proxy identity checks with the target connection's TLS settings when forwarding through an HTTPS proxy.

    HTTPSConnection no longer applies target SNI, assertions, or client credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and continues to use its ssl_context as a fallback when an HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target. (#5093)

  • Fixed URL parsing to more strictly enforce RFC 3986 host syntax, rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters, malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel targets. Host normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization rules for percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved characters and uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained percent-encoded octets. (#5095)

Changelog

title: docs: fix dead Web3 API and portal client links in the book
body:
## Summary
Three outbound links on Nimbus book pages return **HTTP 404** on `unstable`:

1. **Web3 API link** (`consensus-light-client.md`, `execution-client.md`): `https://ethereum.github.io/execution-apis/api-documentation/` is gone. The execution-apis site is now built with Docusaurus (`baseUrl: '/execution-apis/'`, docs at `routeBasePath: '/'`), so the JSON-RPC method reference sits at the site root, `https://ethereum.github.io/execution-apis/`.
2. **fluffy repo link** (`index.md`): `status-im/nimbus-eth1/tree/master/fluffy` 404s because fluffy was renamed to `portal` / `nimbus_portal_client` in status-im/nimbus-eth1#3289. The link now points to `tree/master/portal`, and the text names the Nimbus Portal client (formerly fluffy). The `fluffy.guide` link still works (it serves "The Nimbus Portal Client Guide") and is left as is.

title: fix: send Unix time in the bid request's Date-Milliseconds header
body:
The gloas `getExecutionPayloadBid` request sends `Date-Milliseconds` from `reqStartedAt = Moment.now()`. On Linux, chronos's `Moment.now()` reads `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` (`chronos/timer.nim`, `fastEpochTimeNano`), so the header holds milliseconds since boot. The builder specs define it as the "Unix timestamp in milliseconds at which the request was sent", and the builder must respond by `Date-Milliseconds` plus `X-Timeout-Ms` ([execution_payload_bid.yaml](https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/blob/main/apis/builder/execution_payload_bid.yaml)). So every request arrives with a deadline already in the past.

This takes `reqStartedAt` from `getTime()` and sends it as Unix milliseconds. `reqStartedAt` is used only for this header; the request timeout is still `awaitWithTimeout`.

Tested on a Kurtosis devnet (mainnet preset, gloas at epoch 1) against Commit-Boost, which derives the builder's deadline from these two headers:

| | v26.10.0 | v26.10.0 + this change |
|---|---|---|
| `Date-Milliseconds` captured at the builder URL | `158772668` (host uptime 158820 s) | `1791327502144` (packet received 22:58:22.144 UTC) |
| deadline Commit-Boost derives | already passed: 204 without asking a builder | 1492-1500 ms of the 1500 ms timeout left, over 120 requests |

On the patched node the request reached the builder, which verified the request auth.

This fixes the deadline only. On its own, a validator still gets no bid from a builder it configured through the keymanager API until #9163 is merged too: without it the request goes to `--payload-builder-url` with that URL's default auth data, not to the builders in the stored config. To reach a builder in this test, the validator client's `--payload-builder-url` used the builder's hostname, routed through Commit-Boost. Even then, v26.10.0's builder skipped every bid for lack of proposer preferences, which #9164 adds on `unstable`. We have not run `unstable` with #9163.

title: fix(sync): use per-entity stale-retry timestamp in SyncDag
body:
## Summary

SyncDag used one shared `downloadsMoment` for the Blocks/Sidecars/Envelopes download
timeouts. A `useDownload` for any single entity reset that shared stamp, pushing the other
entities' 12s stale-retry windows back and delaying their retries.

## Root cause

In `beacon_chain/sync/sync_dag.nim`, `SyncDagEntryRef.downloadsMoment` was a single
`chronos.Moment`. `downloadAvailable(d)` measured the timeout against it while `useDownload(d)`
wrote `Moment.now()` to it regardless of `d`.

## Fix

- `downloadsMoment*: array[DagEntity, chronos.Moment]`
- index it with `d` in `downloadAvailable` and `useDownload`
- `debugJsonDump` now reports `last_download` as a 3-element array [Blocks, Sidecars, Envelopes]

Default-init value (epoch `Moment`) keeps the existing "available at init" behavior.

## Test plan

- New regression test in `tests/test_sync_dag.nim`: saturate Blocks count and let its window
  elapse, `useDownload(Sidecars)`, assert `downloadAvailable(Blocks)` stays true and Sidecars
  count == 1; also assert an entity's own `useDownload` still resets its own timestamp.
- Run: `nim test tests/test_sync_dag.nim` (or the repo's sync test target).

title: lock the beacon node and slashing protection databases exclusively
body:
Closes #8954.

The pragma on its own is not enough, because SQLite only takes the lock when the connection first writes, so a second node could still slip in during startup. The empty write transaction after each open is what forces the lock, so the refusal lands at the open with a message that says what happened. It is set at the two opens rather than through `SQLITE_DEFAULT_LOCKING_MODE` so the other tools linking the same wrapper keep their current behaviour.

Worth being explicit about what this does not cover. A node on an older build still uses normal locking and can join a database nobody has locked yet, and the lock is per file, so nothing here stops two nodes with separate data dirs from sharing validator keys. `ncli_db` and `slashingdb export` can no longer read a live node's database, which is the trade I asked about in the issue.

🤖 AI agent (Claude Code / Opus 5) on behalf of @zexoverz

title: Avoid ignoring bids for second Gloas payload building on Fulu
body:
When the second Gloas payload builds on top of the last Fulu payload (e.g., the first Gloas payload was unavailable), we can't reliably get parent gas limit as that's in Fulu, unless we load the full block (DB).

The forkyState.data.latest_execution_payload_bid.gas_limit value is wrong in that situation, so we'd ignore correct bids. And when Gloas finalizes, the value isn't used anymore because we then have the info. Drop the check to avoid risk around the fork transition. If we forward erroneously, it might lead to others ignoring it, but not rejecting.

title: Handle restart when first slot of finalized epoch was missed
body:
When first slot of finalized epoch is missed, the finalized checkpoint block is from a prior epoch. When node is restarted, we initialize the finalizedEpoch from the finalized checkpoint block's slot's epoch, which is incorrect. When we then advertise this as a STATUS message, other peers verify whether our finalized_root is the last block at or before our advertised finalized_epoch.start_slot. As finalized_block.slot is after that, we get disconnected by other peers who see that STATUS.

Change init logic to initialize finalized_epoch based on finalized_block advanced to the next epoch boundary. Also fix AttestationPool init to a proper value as fast confirmation rule logic expects that, and clean up fork choice init logs the print the proper fork choice checkpoints.
author: etan-status

title: Handle STATUS message with finalized_epoch > head_slot.epoch
body:
If the first slot of epoch was missed, the `Checkpoint` for that epoch contains a block root from an earlier epoch. When someone initializes with checkpoint sync from that Checkpoint, their STATUS message is:

- finalized_root: Checkpoint.root
- finalized_epoch: Checkpoint.epoch
- head_root: Checkpoint.root
- head_slot: Checkpoint.root's corresponding block slot

Because Checkpoint.root is from an earlier epoch (as Checkpoint.epoch's initial slot was missed), this means head_slot.epoch < finalized_epoch. Handle that case and don't reject fresh checkpoint synced peers.

title: fix: stop penalizing peers for data columns of invalid or unclaimed blocks
body:
Fixes #9287. By-root column requests for roots in the global `missingSidecars` set (blocks from gossip that no peer advertised, such as an invalid block and its children) no longer score empty responses with `PeerScoreNoValues`; empty responses are only penalized when the root is on the peer's head chain, and a peer that returned nothing for an unclaimed root is not asked for it again while it stays missing. Columns received by root are now KZG-verified on receipt, so a peer sending bad columns is penalized right there, and when `verifyBlock` still returns `Invalid` the block itself is at fault: it is dropped from the quarantines and the missing tables instead of costing the serving peer `PeerScoreBadValues` and being re-downloaded from every other peer. An `Invalid` block fetched by root is likewise removed from `quarantine.missing` so it is not requested from each peer in turn. With the reproduction in #9287, v26.10.0 had 86 low-score peer disconnects in ~30 minutes and both nimbus nodes ended up forked with 1-2 peers; this branch had none from by-root sync and both nodes stayed on the canonical chain.

| reproduction from #9287 (~30 min) | v26.10.0 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| low-score disconnects from by-root sync | 76 and rising (both nimbus nodes) | 0 |
| penalized empty column responses | 580 | 0 (12 empty responses in total, none penalized) |
| nimbus heads | both forked with 1-2 peers, one stuck for 15+ min | canonical; one node lagged a few slots and caught up |

title: Use correct fork for sending ProposerPreferences at transition
body:
For validators running inside the beacon node, when transitioning from a fork to the next, ProposerPreferences are sent an epoch early, e.g., the HEZE_FORK_EPOCH ones are sent during the last Gloas epoch.

These were signed with the current epoch's fork. Correct this to sign them with the correct proposal epoch instead. Also start sending in the last Fulu epoch, as the validator client does.

title: fix(sync): restore Gloas sidecar download counters on request failure
body:
When a Gloas sidecars-by-root request returns an error, `doRootSidecarsSyncStep` restores the Sidecars download counters for `request.fork1.idents` (Fulu), although the failed request used `request.fork2.idents` (Gloas).

This leaves the failed Gloas roots' download counters reserved and can delay retries once the concurrent-download limit is reached. If the same batch also contains Fulu roots, their counters are decremented instead, even though their request succeeded.

Iterate over `request.fork2.idents` in the Gloas error handler so the counters are restored for the roots that were actually requested.

title: fix: preserve execution budget for early Fulu blocks
body:
## Problem

An admissible Fulu block can arrive shortly before its slot starts. During the
preceding slot's last second, `nextSlotDeadline` derives a cutoff that has
already elapsed and returns zero. The Engine API request can then be cancelled
before a response is available. The cached absent result is subsequently
consumed as not validated.

For example, a block arriving 400 ms before slot S currently gets a cutoff
1 second before S, rather than a usable execution budget for S.

## Change

Use the block slot for Fulu's early execution check and direct-storage path.
Clamp the deadline slot to `[wallSlot, wallSlot + 1]` before converting it to
time. This keeps old/current-block behavior, prevents an arbitrary future slot
from creating an unbounded wait, and leaves other fork paths unchanged.

This does not change validity decisions, admission checks, cancellation, retry,
or cache policy.

## Verification

- The new early-slot regression fails against the original arithmetic and
  passes with this change.
- Deterministic tests cover early arrival, exact slot start, current and late
  blocks, the cutoff and its immediate neighbors, and `FAR_FUTURE_SLOT`.
- All three deadline tests pass on both minimal and mainnet presets.
- The full mainnet `test_block_processor` suite passes: 15/15.
- The minimal suite is 11/15. Four unchanged tests fail with the same
  Bellatrix/Capella `FieldDefect` before and after this change: Reverse order
  block add & get, Multiple heads, Invalidate block root, and Invalidate existing
  block root. None was edited, skipped, or disabled.
- `make -j4 nimbus_beacon_node` succeeds.

Test compilation used `./env.sh nim c -d:release -d:disableLTO
-d:const_preset=<preset> --out:<binary> tests/test_block_processor.nim`.
The full mainnet binary was run without a filter. Individual regressions were
also run using the runner's exact `suite::test` names.

On the same mainnet node, without changing the execution client or resource
limits, a before/after observation showed:

| Observation | Before | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Optimistic REST samples | 26/180 | 0/768 |
| Longest observed optimistic run | 22 seconds | 0 seconds |
| Early blocks examined | 24, all NOT_VALIDATED | 7 resolved before slot start, all VALID |

The patched observation collected 768 samples at a one-second cadence
(768 seconds on the process monotonic clock). All 59
resolved blocks were VALID, finalized epoch advanced by two, and there were no
API errors, EL-offline samples, logged errors, or process restarts. There were
15 brief syncing samples with maximum sync distance one slot. These are
observations from one node, not a general performance guarantee.

Checked `stable`, `testing`, and `unstable` before submission: each still uses
the wall-slot-only helper.

title: Cache PTC in EpochRef
body:
Payload attestation messages need to look up the PTC depending on the branch that they arrive on, which may have different PTC shufflings, akin to regular attestation messages. Cache PTC in EpochRef so that gossip rules are enforced correctly in branching non-finality scenarios.

Note findEpochRef does not trigger state replays, if it's not there it simply returns none.
