title: Prune data columns of orphaned blocks
body:
When finalization prunes a block that didn't make it into the canonical chain, `pruneBlockSlot` deletes the block (and, for Gloas, its payload envelope), but its data column sidecars were left in the database. Slot-based column pruning only ever finds the canonical block of a slot, so these rows were never deleted.

This deletes the columns together with the block, for Fulu and later. This applies in every history mode, like the deletion of the block itself.

Fixes #9401

**Testing**

- New test "columns of orphaned blocks are pruned on finalization" (suite "Data column pruning" in `test_blockchain_dag.nim`): a block on a fork keeps its columns until finalization rules it out, then they are deleted, while the canonical block of the same slot keeps its columns. The test fails without the fix.
- Not tested on a live node.

**Note**

In Gloas, `storePayload` stores the columns only after `addHeadExecutionPayload`, a head update and an `await` on the execution head update. If finalization prunes the block within that window, its columns are written after it is gone and are not cleaned up. This needs a block on a fork that finality rules out at exactly that point; it is not addressed here - a check that the block is still known before storing would close it.
author: smithmid

title: Catch up on data column pruning after downtime
body:
Builds on #9403 (prune data columns of orphaned blocks) - only the second commit is new here. Once #9403 is merged, I'll rebase this onto `unstable`, which drops the first commit.

Data column pruning only looked at the one slot leaving the retention window on each slot end, so the columns of every slot that passed without a slot end - while the node was offline, or when slot processing fell behind and jumped ahead - were never deleted. This keeps the pruning position in the database and continues from it.

Fixes #9402

**Changes**

- The position is stored under a new key, `kDataColumnPruneSlot`: columns before that slot have been pruned. Without a record (first start after upgrading, or a new database), pruning starts at the current retention boundary.
- Each call scans at most an epoch of slots and prunes at most two blocks' columns, in one transaction, so catching up after a long outage doesn't cause lag spikes.
- While the node isn't synced, pruning also runs whenever sync stores columns, so it keeps pace with sync instead of with the slot clock. Without this, catching up after an outage writes columns far faster than one pruning step per slot removes the expired ones, and the database grows by about the outage's worth of columns (it is never vacuumed, so it doesn't shrink back). Once synced, pruning only runs at slot end as before. Neither runs with `--history=column-archive`.
- The retention window is measured from `min(wall slot, head slot)`. A wall clock that is too far ahead can otherwise delete columns that are still in the window, which can't be undone. The trade-off is that while the head is stalled, expired columns stay a little longer. This also keeps pruning before the head, where `getBlockRange` can't find a block yet.
- This replaces the special case for the last slot of each epoch: `onSlotEnd` still skips pruning on it, and the next call catches up.
- Pruning moves from `nimbus_beacon_node.nim` to `ChainDAGRef`, next to `pruneHistory`, so that it can be tested without a full `BeaconNode`. `pruneDataColumnsAtSlot` is unchanged apart from operating on the DAG and returning whether it deleted anything.

**Not covered**

- Rows that leaked before this change, from orphaned blocks or downtime, are not cleaned up: pruning starts at the current boundary rather than walking the whole history. As the database isn't vacuumed, deleting them would also not shrink the file - only a resync gets that space back.
- After switching from `--history=column-archive` back to pruning, a node that pruned before continues from where it stopped, and the backlog clears at about one block per slot. A node that never pruned has no saved position, so pruning starts at the current boundary and the columns it archived stay, as before this change.
- A narrow case remains with the column reconstruction backfiller, which only runs on nodes custodying at least half of the columns: it stores its result after an `await` on the reconstruction, and if the head moves on by more than an epoch meanwhile, which in practice only happens during sync, pruning may already have passed that slot. Checking the slot against the backfiller's retention window again before storing would close it.

**Testing**

- New test "catches up on missed slots in bounded steps" (suite "Data column pruning" in `test_blockchain_dag.nim`): starting point without a record, the per-call limits, a run of empty slots longer than an epoch, catching up to the target, and a wall clock far ahead of the head.
- New test "data column prune slot" in `test_beacon_chain_db.nim`: the key round-trips.
- Mutation testing: each of these changes makes the new tests fail - not deleting orphan columns, measuring the window from the wall clock only, pruning three blocks per call, scanning two epochs per call, starting from genesis without a record, and not saving the position.
- Not tested on a live node.

title: fix(vc): submit sync committee selections for current slot only
body:
## Summary
- Restrict VC sync committee selection proof filling to the **current slot only** (drop the `N..N+2` prefetch window).
- Aligns with [ethereum/beacon-APIs#675](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/675): `POST /eth/v1/validator/sync_committee_selections` must only contain selections for the current slot.
- Fixes distributed-validator failures against Charon: prefetching future slots meant requests never reached threshold before the middleware timeout, so contributions were signed with partial proofs and rejected.  Nimbus will now be in alignment with all other clients

Fixes #9172

## Problem
With `--distributed`, the VC prefetched sync committee selection proofs for slots `N..N+2`. After the first request, slots with a stored partial proof were skipped, so later calls typically only contained `N+2`. Other operators (and Charon) only exchange the **current** slot, so `N+2` never reached threshold before Charon’s ~10s timeout (resulting in a `408 client cancelled request` error). The VC then published sync contributions with its own partial selection proof; Charon rejected them (`signature not verified`), and the Nimbus operator missed sync contribution shares.

Beacon committee selections were largely fine because attester duties are sparse; sync committee members need a selection every slot, so the multi-slot prefetch always hurt.

There is also no benefit to prefetching sync selections: sync committee subnet subscriptions have no aggregator flag and last the whole period, so the (aggregated) proof is only needed in the duty slot itself. Other VCs (Lighthouse, Lodestar, Prysm, Teku) already send current-slot-only.

## Approach
- Change `getSyncCommitteeDutiesRequests` / `fillSyncCommitteeSelectionProofs` to take a single `slot` (remove the range API).
- `fillSyncCommitteeSelections` in the duties service calls that single-slot API.
- Attestation selection prefetch (`AGGREGATION_PRE_COMPUTE_SLOTS`) is unchanged (aggregator flag / committee subnet subscriptions).

## Test plan
- [x] Unit test in `tests/test_validator_client.nim`: `fillSyncCommitteeSelectionProofs only fills the duty slot` (proofs for the duty slot only; not `+1` / `+2`)
- [x] Updated `AllTests-mainnet.md`
- [x] Ran targeted `test_validator_client` in Docker (`nimbus-vctest`): 1 OK
- [ ] CI unit suite

## AI assistance disclosure
I used AI (Cursor) to help inspect the VC sync selection path, compare beacon-APIs#675 / client behavior summarized on ethereum/beacon-APIs#666, draft this patch, run the Docker unit test, and prepare this PR text. I reviewed the resulting diff and can explain the change. A human author remains responsible for the submitted code.  I am a node operator rather than a regular Nimbus contributor; corrections from maintainers are welcome.
